entries.title: Summary mode is three lengths of plain words
entries.body: Summary mode shows the piece in plain words at one of three lengths, Brief, Simple and Fuller, chosen with a slider. The icons at either end of the slider jump straight to Brief or Fuller, and the panel is a little wider on wide screens. The outline of parts and sections has gone from Summary, because Structure mode already shows it; old links to that outline open the Simple summary.

entries.title: Chat is told which passages are on screen
entries.body: When you send a question in Chat, or save an edit to one, the AI is told which passages were on your screen at that moment, marked as context only. If your question is about what you are looking at, that helps it answer; if not, it is told to ignore it. Before, it knew only roughly where you were.

entries.title: Investigate in Citations becomes Dig deeper
entries.body: In Citations, the button beneath each cited work, shown to the article's owner, is called Dig deeper, as it is in the Glossary and in comments. Every press starts with a web search before any answer, and the answer is written by a more capable AI with more room, so it is less likely to be cut off.

entries.title: Summaries and Tweets leave out the paperwork
entries.body: New and refreshed summaries and Tweets threads skip acknowledgements, conflicts of interest and author affiliations, and finish on the piece's own conclusion. A Brief summary aims for 80 words in two short paragraphs. Structure keeps that paperwork as one short, labelled entry rather than dropping it.

entries.title: A slow article load shows the animated logo
entries.body: When an article takes a moment to load, the page shows a large Spideryarn logo in the middle, its spider and letters cycling through their animations, in place of a line of text. If your device is set to reduce motion you see the sentence as before, and screen readers still read it out.

entries.title: This page describes the version you are using
entries.body: Notes on this page used to be written after each release and appear with the next one, so the list ran one release behind. They are published with the release itself, and the line warning that the list might lag has gone.

entries.title: Tables in PDFs show their contents
entries.body: Every table in an imported PDF reached you as a caption over nothing. The table's cells appear beneath its caption, checked for errors the same way as the rest of the text. This applies to PDFs added or reprocessed from this release on.

entries.title: Dictation uses your computer's default microphone
entries.body: In Chrome and similar browsers, with no microphone picked, dictation and Live conversation could open the browser's own default microphone rather than the one your computer uses. They ask for the system default, and while dictation is on its strip names the microphone in use. If a chosen microphone is missing, both try the system default and tell you.
